title: Predators & prey: top-down or bottom-up?
sub: Symposium topic 3 · Krebs et al. 1995 vs Oli et al. 2026
blurb: Snowshoe hare cycles in Yukon: predation, food, trophic cascades.
lede: Group 3's question: top-down control or bottom-up release? The test case is the snowshoe hare cycle in Kluane, Yukon. Classic: Krebs et al. (1995). Recent: Oli et al. (2026).
six: **Top-down control**: consumers (predators) regulate the lower trophic levels.
**Bottom-up control**: resource supply (food, nutrients, plant productivity) sets the higher levels.
**Predation** in the glossary is broad: anything that reduces prey's future survival or reproduction to zero (parasitoids, herbivory, seed predation too).
**Trophic cascade**: a change at one level ripples down, with alternating rises and falls in biomass.
Krebs 1995: food addition AND predator exclusion together gave the biggest effect (~11×), but the decline still came.
Oli 2026: 43 years of capture-mark-recapture; declines come from lower survival, mainly before weaning. Verdict: predation matters a lot, but food and demography matter too.
foot: Source: Group 3 symposium slides; glossary section 4.

questions.answer: Consumers mainly regulate the lower trophic levels
wrong: Resources mainly regulate the higher levels

questions.answer: Resource supply mainly determines the higher trophic levels

questions.q: Which of these counts as predation under the glossary's broad definition?
questions.answer: A parasitoid that inevitably kills its host
wrong: A bird nesting in a tree
questions.e: Predation reduces prey's future survival or reproduction to zero; includes parasitoids, parasitic castration, herbivory and seed predation.

questions.answer: Effects passing down a food web, with alternating rises and falls in biomass
wrong: A single predator eating many prey
questions.e: E.g. more predators → fewer herbivores → more plants.

questions.q: How long is the snowshoe hare population cycle?
questions.e: Numbers grow very large, then crash sharply.

questions.q: Where were both hare studies done?
Which Krebs et al. 1995 treatment gave the biggest increase in hare density?
Why did the hare decline still happen in the Krebs experiment?
questions.answer: Birds of prey still hunted and hares could leave the fenced areas
questions.e: The decline was delayed, not prevented.

questions.q: What method did Oli et al. 2026 use?
questions.answer: Capture-mark-recapture models on 43 years of data
questions.e: Data 1977–2020, more than 20,000 captures of over 7,000 hares.

questions.q: What mainly drove population declines in Oli et al. 2026?
questions.e: Survival was higher in the increase phase.

questions.q: In the hare food web, the hares are…
Risk-induced stress and behaviour changes in prey are…
questions.e: Lethal = killing; non-lethal = fear, stress, behaviour shifts.

questions.answer: Predation plays a major role, but food and demographic processes are also essential
questions.e: The two studies give complementary evidence.

vocab.meaning: Consumers (predators, herbivores) mainly regulate the lower trophic levels.
Resource supply (nutrients, primary production) mainly determines the higher trophic levels.
Direct and indirect effects passing down a food web, with alternating rises and falls in biomass.
Interaction that reduces prey's future survival or reproduction to zero.
An organism that develops on a host and inevitably kills it.
Fear, stress and behaviour changes caused by predation risk.
Catching, marking and recatching animals to estimate survival and population size.

facts: The snowshoe hare cycle lasts about {10|2|50|100} years.
Food plus predator exclusion raised hare density about {11|2|100|50} times.
Oli et al. found declines come mainly from lower survival before {weaning|winter|birth|migration}.
